stories.headline: Brent sinks to [$91.7] as surplus looms
stories.summary: Brent crude slipped 0.2% to $91.70 a barrel on Thursday, 19 Nov, and US WTI fell 0.7% to $82.70. WTI had dropped 3.2% the day before to its lowest since 26 August. US crude stocks rose 3.4 million barrels, and Hormuz shipments have recovered to near pre-war levels, raising fears of oversupply.

stories.headline: Tanker hit in engine room - [crew all safe]
stories.summary: An outbound tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in its engine room about 6 nm north of Khasab, Oman, at 1645 UTC on 18 Nov. All crew were reported safe and accounted for. The day before, ADNOC's product tanker Navig8 Messi was hit nearby; 11 crew were injured and the search for one missing seafarer continues.

stories.headline: Hacker claims data of [54,000 Filipino seafarers]
stories.summary: Cyber group Deep Web Konek warned that a hacker called "mrhansolo" claims to have breached Seaker, a platform used by Filipino mariners, manning agencies and maritime schools. The hacker says about 54,167 people are affected, with passport details, seafarer documents, addresses and phone numbers. The data is offered for $1,300 - the claim is not yet confirmed.

stories.headline: GPS jamming - crews told to [use paper charts]
stories.summary: The UK Maritime and Coastguard Agency has advised shipping companies to plan for operating without GPS as Iran is suspected of jamming and spoofing signals in Hormuz. A UK hearing heard that 970 ships a day were jammed in June. Crews are urged to refresh chart navigation skills and Morse flashing-light signalling.

stories.headline: Modi launches [Seafarers' Safety Initiative] in Manila
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a Seafarers' Safety Initiative at the 21st East Asia Summit in Manila on 17 Nov. It aims to boost cooperation between East Asia Summit nations on joint training and emergency response for seafarers. Attacks on merchant ships in West Asia and the Black Sea have killed several Indian seafarers.

stories.headline: Crimean Bridge span falls - [Kerch channel blocked]
stories.summary: The road arch and span of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the Kerch Strait overnight on 17 Nov, reportedly blocking the shipping channel. Clearing the heavy wreck needs special equipment and complex underwater work and could take a long time. The Kerch Strait links the Sea of Azov to the Black Sea for grain ships.

stories.headline: Mozambique approves [$30bn Rovuma LNG] plan
stories.summary: Mozambique's Council of Ministers approved ExxonMobil's amended Rovuma LNG development plan on 17 Nov. Capacity rises to 18.6 million tonnes a year from 15.2 mtpa approved in 2019, and the cost could be close to $30 billion. Exxon targets a final investment decision by end-2026, with output possible in the early 2030s.

stories.headline: Hafnia [drops Torm merger], hands out stake
stories.summary: Product tanker owner Hafnia has dropped its attempt to merge with rival Torm. It plans to give its 19.85% Torm stake to its own shareholders as a special dividend, one Torm share per 26.3 Hafnia shares. Hafnia will also spend $235 million on purchase options for eight tankers. Q3 net profit was $170.8 million.

stories.headline: HD Hyundai wins [4 LPG carriers] for $200m
stories.summary: HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering won an order for four LPG carriers worth 272.1 billion won, about $200 million, from an Oceania-based owner. Brokers link the order to Greece's Naftomar for 9,000 cbm semi-refrigerated ships. They will be built at Ulsan and delivered by the second half of 2029.
